html:
American industrialist who founded the Ford Motor Company in 1903 and made the car something ordinary families could buy. Raised on a farm near Detroit, he became chief engineer at the Edison Illuminating Company in Detroit and built his first car in 1896.

His great product was the Model T of 1908. To make it cheaply he brought in the moving assembly line at his Highland Park plant in 1913, borrowing ideas from the meatpacking lines of places like the Union Stock Yards. Car prices fell year after year.

In 1914 he doubled the pay of many workers to five dollars a day, to cut turnover and help them afford the cars they made. This mix of mass production, high wages and mass buying became known as Fordism.

He also had a dark side. He fought labour unions, sometimes with violence. His newspaper, the Dearborn Independent, spread antisemitic articles in the 1920s that were reprinted around the world and admired by the Nazis.
